title: A genome-wide in vivo CRISPR screen identifies essential regulators of T cell migration to the CNS in a multiple sclerosis model
model: Encephalitogenic Lewis rat CD4+ T-MBP cells, genome-wide (87,690 guides) and validation (12,000 guides) knockout libraries, in vivo transfer
contrast: T cells in spinal-cord parenchyma (and meninges) vs blood, day 3, paired by animal (3 vs 3)
paper_calls: 22 (parenchyma) and 9 (meninges) genes at FDR 0.10 in the genome-wide screen; 20 in the validation screen; Itga4, Cxcr3, Fermt3, Grk2, Cbfb among the top
barcs_calls: 0 genes at FDR 0.10 in the genome-wide screen (hits top-ranked but not significant with 2 residual df); 22 in the validation screen
named_hits: Genome-wide: Itga4 #1, Grk2 #8, Fermt3 #12, Cxcr3 #30, all depleted but not FDR-significant. Validation: all 5 at FDR 0.10 (Itga4 #1 FDR 4e-9, Cxcr3 #3, Fermt3 #4, Grk2 #7, Cbfb #12)
verdict: BARCS ranks the paper's validated migration hits (Itga4, Cxcr3, Fermt3, Grk2) at the very top of the noisy genome-wide screen but calls nothing at FDR 0.10 there with 2 residual df; the validation screen confirms all five at FDR 0.10.
